text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: private-cluster gpu-queue growth > 250 for customer: oakridge (region: eu-west-1). Autoscaler error rate spike. Investigate.
aaron.s: seeing huge queue growth on oakridge private cluster. GPU utilization ~99%. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to provision nodes, error: 'ImagePullBackOff' on provisioning pod. Paging oncall.
maya.p: confirming. customer reported latency spikes ~10x for model r6-7b. CS already got a ticket. I'll join.
aaron.s: grabbing autoscaler logs now. early grep:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z autoscaler-manager ERROR provisioner.go:421 failed to create node: rpc error: code=13 desc="failed to pull image: unauthorized"
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z autoscaler-manager WARN backoff: retrying provisioning in 30s
```
maya.p: that explains nodes not coming up. looks like the private registry creds expired on customer side or our node bootstrap can't access it. but why did this start suddenly? no config changes from our side in last 24h.
aaron.s: checking kubelet logs on control plane; also seeing taint mismatch warnings that cause pods to stay pending even when nodes appear in cluster. so two problems: image pull auth + tolerations mismatch for our provisioner pods.
sre-lead-julie: assign triage. aaron you own oncall for now. maya can you validate impact and tell CS what to say to customer? cs-ella: on it, I'll draft message.
maya.p: rough customer impact: generation latency > 8s for user-facing endpoints, ~40% requests getting 429 throttles as the internal queue hits per-customer limit. customers with dedicated capacity unaffected. this is the private/vpc cluster only.
cs-ella: cc @oakridge - we're investigating. will update in 30m. suggest telling them we see an auth failure for provisioning images and are doing a manual remediation.
aaron.s: attempting manual node creation via cloud control-plane with temporary image override (use public fallback image) to drain queue. command I'm about to run:
```
kubectl apply -f nodepool-fallback.yaml --context=oakridge
# nodepool-fallback.yaml uses public-registry image and relaxed tolerations for provisioning-agent
```
ops-bot: manual node creation requested by aaron.s: job id 6621 queued. note: will apply firewall rules - may take 90-120s to boot.
maya.p: while that boots, can we route high-priority traffic to hosted fallback? we have policy to route to hosted for severe private outages.
aaron.s: yes we can. starting traffic reroute policy for oakridge to use hosted-fast variant for critical routes. This will slightly increase costs but preserves SLA. command:
```
redwoodctl route set --customer oakridge --fallback hosted-fast --priority critical
```
oncall-next-kim: picking up monitoring for fallout after handoff. will stand by for metrics.
aaron.s: created the fallback nodes (3 GPU nodes) with public image. they showed up but kubelet reports kubelet version mismatch for the provisioning agent; still trying to make them join; patching daemonset tolerations now.
maya.p: traffic reroute started :white_check_mark: 35% of critical traffic now on hosted-fast. CS, please let customer know 35% routed away and rest is queued but being processed.
cs-ella: message sent to oakridge: "We're routing a portion of traffic to our hosted fallback and executing manual node provisioning to restore capacity. Expect incremental improvement in 15-30 minutes. We'll follow up when full capacity is restored."
aaron.s: nailed the tolerations patch. nodes are in Ready. starting to drain queue. Observability shows GPU queue size trending down from 260 -> 120.
maya.p: nice. still seeing intermittent 429s for non-critical routes, but critical are stable.
sre-lead-julie: good mitigation. next steps: (1) rotate registry creds for private bootstrap and add preflight check to autoscaler, (2) add toleration compatibility test to image builds, (3) runbook update for immediate manual fallback path. aaron can you open post-incident ticket?
aaron.s: opening P1 -> INC-2613456789 in pager duty and tagging eng-infra. I'll include timestamps, logs, and commands used. also adding a quick mitigation script to runbook.
incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-2613456789. Severity: page. Owners: aaron.s (oncall), julie (sre lead).
ops-bot: note: nodepool-fallback used different instance type (a100->a10) due to capacity limits; performance will be slightly degraded. logged.
maya.p: customer impact summary for postmortem draft: 1) private cluster provisioning blocked by registry auth error causing autoscaler backoff; 2) node taint/toleration mismatch prevented some agents from joining; 3) result: queue growth -> request throttling and increased latency for oakridge for ~45 minutes. mitigation: manual node creation with public image + toleration patch, plus traffic routing to hosted fallback.
cs-ella: customer follow-up: oakridge asked for root cause and ETA for permanent fix. I've told them we'll do creds rotation and a runbook update; they'll want an after-action within 48 hours. I'll log that in INC ticket.
aaron.s: quick notes I'm adding to ticket: logs, the exact autoscaler error lines, the kubectl snippets, and the change to routing policy. also scheduled a meeting with infra team to discuss why registry creds expired without alert.
oncall-next-kim: taking handoff at 2026-03-15T11:00Z. will monitor metrics and alert if queue > 200 again. leaving handoff note in incident channel.
sre-lead-julie: post-incident action items assigned: infra to add registry credential health probe (P1), autoscaler to check preflight image pull (P2), devex to write toleration validation in CI (P2). we'll run blameless postmortem.
maya.p: current status: queue at 18, latency normalizing, no new 429s for critical. good to close page if stable for 30m.
aaron.s: copying final commands used for runbook:
```
# fallback route
redwoodctl route set --customer oakridge --fallback hosted-fast --priority critical
# manual node create
kubectl apply -f nodepool-fallback.yaml --context=oakridge
# toleration patch
kubectl patch daemonset provisioning-agent -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"node.kubernetes.io/unreachable","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoExecute"}]}}}}'
```
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED: queue draining < 50 for 30m. postmortem requested.
cs-ella: sent final update to customer and scheduled 1:1 with oakridge to review remediation plan.
oncall-next-kim: confirming I'll keep watch for 2 hours then revert routing if stable.
sre-lead-julie: thanks team. postmortem owner: aaron.s. target: 72h deliverable with RCA and fixes. closing thread here and moving details into INC-2613456789.
aaron.s: :thumbsup: thanks all for quick turnaround.
